provisions.summary: Raises the Hawaii standard deduction in steps: for 2027 the amounts are $16,000 joint / $12,000 head of household / $8,000 single (from the after-2025 tier), rising in later tiers to $18,000/$13,500/$9,000 (after 2027), $20,000/$15,000/$10,000 (after 2029) and $24,000/$18,000/$12,000 (after 2030). Because the amounts differ across 2027-2031, they are not modeled.
provisions.quote: For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027: (i) $18,000 in the case of a joint return as provided by section 235-93

provisions.summary: Replaces the income tax bracket schedules for joint filers and surviving spouses (subsection (a)) with schedules that widen brackets for tax years after 2024, 2026 and 2028. The 2027 and 2029 vintages are modeled.
provisions.quote: In the case of any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028: If the taxable income is: The tax shall be: Not over $38,400 1.40% of taxable income

provisions.summary: Replaces the income tax bracket schedules for heads of household (subsection (b)) with widened schedules for tax years after 2024, 2026 and 2028.
provisions.quote: In the case of any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028: If the taxable income is: The tax shall be: Not over $28,800 1.40% of taxable income

provisions.summary: Replaces the income tax bracket schedules for single filers and married individuals filing separately (subsection (c)) with widened schedules for tax years after 2024, 2026 and 2028.
provisions.quote: In the case of any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028: If the taxable income is: The tax shall be: Not over $19,200 1.40% of taxable income

notes: This is a 2024-session bill (HB2404 CD1) written against pre-Act 24 law. Its first-effect year is tax year 2024, but the spec models tax years 2027-2031 only, so first_year is 2027. Standard deduction: the bill sets different amounts for tax years 2026, 2028, 2030 and 2031 (and so for different years within 2027-2031), so under rule 6 it is left out of the spec and listed as not modeled. The 2027 schedule is the one headed 'after December 31, 2026'; it stays in force through 2028, and the 'after December 31, 2028' schedule applies from 2029 through 2031. The bill does not touch the capital gains alternative tax, the EITC or the food/excise credit, so those stay at current law (Act 24, SLH 2026). Section 4 makes the Act apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2023 (an applicability provision, not listed). Married filing separately uses the single schedule, which matches subsection (c).
